## Story-level uncertainties

- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the father is identified with a prophet of Madyan, and the women and their father are given names in later works.
- The man in these ayat is not named in them; linking him to a person of the same surah is an inference from the context.
- Hadith to add later: reports about the women of Madyan and their father, with a named grader for each; none is used here.

## How to review

1. Verses: do the listed ayat really contain what each claim says? Is any claim stronger than its ayat?
2. Pronouns and speakers: where the Arabic names none, does the draft say so?
3. Words with more than one reading: decide how the page words each.
4. Omissions: anything the verses say that readers need and the chapter leaves out?
5. No added facts: no name, number, place, reason, emotion or sequence beyond the ayat; no implied chronology.
6. No depiction of any prophet, angel or jinn.
7. Theology and etiquette: cautious wording about prophets; no verdicts; no legal or medical ruling.
8. Kids mode only restates the claims; nothing frightening or misleading.
9. Lessons are marked as interpretation and are modest; none reads as scripture or a promise.
10. Unknowns and tradition: each 'Named in later tradition' line is accurate and only a label.
11. Titles and honorifics: bare names in the draft; honorifics added at render time.
12. Sign-off goes in the platform review flow (name, version, decision), not in this file.

## 1. At the water of Madyan  (`#at-the-water-of-madyan`)

Cited ayat: 28:23-28

> **28:23** وَلَمَّا وَرَدَ مَآءَ مَدْيَنَ وَجَدَ عَلَيْهِ أُمَّةً مِّنَ ٱلنَّاسِ يَسْقُونَ وَوَجَدَ مِن دُونِهِمُ ٱمْرَأَتَيْنِ تَذُودَانِ قَالَ مَا خَطْبُكُمَا قَالَتَا لَا نَسْقِى حَتَّىٰ يُصْدِرَ ٱلرِّعَآءُ وَأَبُونَا شَيْخٌ كَبِيرٌ
>
> **28:24** فَسَقَىٰ لَهُمَا ثُمَّ تَوَلَّىٰٓ إِلَى ٱلظِّلِّ فَقَالَ رَبِّ إِنِّى لِمَآ أَنزَلْتَ إِلَىَّ مِنْ خَيْرٍ فَقِيرٌ
>
> **28:25** فَجَآءَتْهُ إِحْدَىٰهُمَا تَمْشِى عَلَى ٱسْتِحْيَآءٍ قَالَتْ إِنَّ أَبِى يَدْعُوكَ لِيَجْزِيَكَ أَجْرَ مَا سَقَيْتَ لَنَا فَلَمَّا جَآءَهُۥ وَقَصَّ عَلَيْهِ ٱلْقَصَصَ قَالَ لَا تَخَفْ نَجَوْتَ مِنَ ٱلْقَوْمِ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
>
> **28:26** قَالَتْ إِحْدَىٰهُمَا يَٰٓأَبَتِ ٱسْتَـْٔجِرْهُ إِنَّ خَيْرَ مَنِ ٱسْتَـْٔجَرْتَ ٱلْقَوِىُّ ٱلْأَمِينُ
>
> **28:27** قَالَ إِنِّىٓ أُرِيدُ أَنْ أُنكِحَكَ إِحْدَى ٱبْنَتَىَّ هَٰتَيْنِ عَلَىٰٓ أَن تَأْجُرَنِى ثَمَٰنِىَ حِجَجٍ فَإِنْ أَتْمَمْتَ عَشْرًا فَمِنْ عِندِكَ وَمَآ أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَشُقَّ عَلَيْكَ سَتَجِدُنِىٓ إِن شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ مِنَ ٱلصَّٰلِحِينَ
>
> **28:28** قَالَ ذَٰلِكَ بَيْنِى وَبَيْنَكَ أَيَّمَا ٱلْأَجَلَيْنِ قَضَيْتُ فَلَا عُدْوَٰنَ عَلَىَّ وَٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ مَا نَقُولُ وَكِيلٌ

### Claims

**c1** (28:23): A man who came to the water of Madyan found there a crowd of people watering, and found apart from them a pair of women holding back, and when he asked what their concern was, they said that they could not water until the shepherds withdrew, since their father was a very old man.

**c2** (28:24): He watered for them, then went back to the shade and said, my Lord, I am in need of whatever good You send down to me.

**c3** (28:25): One of them came to him with modesty and said that her father was calling him to repay him for watering for them, and when he came to her father and told him his account, the father said, do not fear, you have escaped from the wrongdoing people.

**c4** (28:26): One of them said to her father that he should hire him, since the best one to hire is the strong and the trustworthy.

**c5** (28:27): The father said that he wished to marry one of these daughters of his to him on condition that he work for him for eight years, and if he completed ten it would be of his own accord, adding that he did not wish to burden him and that he would find him, if God willed, among the righteous.

**c6** (28:28): The man answered that this was agreed between them, that whichever term he completed there would be no wrong against him, and that God was a guardian over what they said.

### One-minute summary

A man came to the water of Madyan and watered for a pair of women who were holding back [c1][c2]. Their father called him, and one of the women said that he should be hired as the strong and trustworthy one [c3][c4]. The father proposed that he work for him for eight years, or ten if he chose, and offered one of his daughters in marriage [c5].

### Complete story

A man who came to the water of Madyan found there a crowd of people watering, and found apart from them a pair of women holding back, and when he asked what their concern was, they said that they could not water until the shepherds withdrew, since their father was a very old man [c1]. He watered for them, then went back to the shade and said, my Lord, I am in need of whatever good You send down to me [c2]. One of them came to him with modesty and said that her father was calling him to repay him for watering for them, and when he came to her father and told him his account, the father said, do not fear, you have escaped from the wrongdoing people [c3]. One of them said to her father that he should hire him, since the best one to hire is the strong and the trustworthy [c4]. The father said that he wished to marry one of these daughters of his to him on condition that he work for him for eight years, and if he completed ten it would be of his own accord, adding that he did not wish to burden him and that he would find him, if God willed, among the righteous [c5]. The man answered that this was agreed between them, that whichever term he completed there would be no wrong against him, and that God was a guardian over what they said [c6].

### Deep study

The ayat name neither the women, their father nor the man [c1]. They record the terms the father offered, eight years with ten as a favour from the man [c5].

### Kids mode

A man came to the water of Madyan [c1]. He saw a pair of women holding back and watered for them [c1][c2]. Their father asked to see him, and one of the women said that he was strong and trustworthy [c3][c4].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that after helping the women the man turned to God and said that he needed whatever good God might send [c2]. Another is that one of the women described the best person to hire as strong and trustworthy [c4].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: the names of the women, their father or the man, or where Madyan lay.
- Not established: the Arabic word in the ayah that is rendered years can also mean pilgrimages, and years is the usual reading.
- Not established: which of the women the father meant, or whether the marriage took place within these ayat; the ayah records the offer and the man's reply.
- Not established: how long the man stayed, or how long the work lasted.
